_comment: Q19c from evals/open-questions.md: does 'call it directly' in the weather description head remove the misses that happen before the first call? Registered before the run.

arms.best: mcpBest with the 'CALL IT DIRECTLY' head (1,776 chars)

protocol: Portable harness (skill references/harness/), 12 waves, 3+3 interleaved, no retries, no rate limits.
headline: Pre-call misses gone: best made a weather call in 30/30 runs; 0 asked for an address (Q19b: 3 of 30). forecast-normalization: calls 10/10 (Q19: 2/10).

Quarter questions hold: weather-partial-normalization best 10/10 (rich 10/10), weather-single-quarter best 9/10 (rich 0/10); 2 correct best answers still annualise after the correct figure, 1 leads with the year.

forecast-normalization: best 5/10 against rich 5/10 on the behaviour scored (noticing the forecast tail). Now that best calls, the miss is downstream: 5 runs quote the correction factor for the whole window without saying 7 days are forecast, although the response's forecast alert says so. Every rich answer applies the annual factor to 30 days (93.96/96.55, often read as a percentage); best 0.

P1.detail: 0 of 20 best runs on the quarter questions asked for an address without calling

P2.detail: best calls in 10/10 (>= 8 met) but is CORRECT in 5/10 (predicted >= 6; falsified at <= 3)

scoring: Q19 rubric + 19 hand verdicts with reasons. forecast-normalization scored on its question's behaviour (the forecast tail noticed and said); the annual-factor-on-30-days error is counted separately because it is not what that question scores.

log_audit.explained: wave 12's window holds 5 extra best rows with queryIntent 'field probe fixture' — the author's own fixture fetches for the field-reading probe, made during that wave. Net of those, exact.

caveats: haiku only, n=10, one sitting; comparisons with Q19/Q19b are cross-sitting (direction only).
Same author for metadata, questions, ground truth and scoring.
